## The lighthouse problem

### Exploratory data analysis

```{r}
# Read in data: 
dat = read.csv('Lecture_2/measurements.csv')
# View(dat)
```

```{r}
hist(dat$x,
     col='lightblue',
     xlab = 'xk',
     main = 'Distance along coastline where flashes are measured.')
```

### Simulate data

```{r}
set.seed(1)

alpha = 3.25
beta  = 0.5

npoints = 100
angles = runif(npoints,-pi/2,pi/2) 

xk = rep(NA,length(angles))
xk[angles<0] = alpha-beta*tan(abs(angles[angles<0]))
xk[angles>0] = alpha+beta*tan(angles[angles>0])
xk[angles==0] = alpha

xk = xk[xk>=0];xk=xk[xk<=5]
```

### Posterior distribution 

```{r}
# Posterior distribution:
# alpha: position along coastline
# beta:  position out to sea
# xk:    data
lhouse_post_fxn = function(alpha,beta,xk) {
  n = length(xk)
  
  llik = length(xk)*log(beta) - sum(log(beta^2+(xk-alpha)^2))
  return(exp(llik)) # returns likelihood 
}

# Vectorize function:
lhouse_post_vfxn = Vectorize(FUN=lhouse_post_fxn,vectorize.args=c('alpha','beta'))
```

### Plotting posterior distribution 

```{r}
alpha_seq = seq(0,5,length=100)
beta_seq  = seq(0.1,2,length=100)

Z = outer(X=alpha_seq,
          Y=beta_seq,
          FUN='lhouse_post_vfxn',
          xk=xk)

contour(alpha_seq,
        beta_seq,
        Z,
        nlevels=10,
        xlab=expression(alpha),
        ylab=expression(beta),
        main='',
        col='deeppink')
points(x=3.25,
       y=0.5,
       col='blue',
       pch=16)
```

## The lighthouse problem 
Here we bound $\theta_{k}$ under the assumption that there is some finite piece of coastline over which the detector operates.
